quotes.text: མདོ་རྒྱན་འགྲེལ་བའི་རྣམ་བཤད་རྣམ་གཉིས་ཀྱི། ། དཀའ་བའི་གནད་རྣམས་གསལ་བར་བྱེད་པ་ཡི། ། མདོ་དང་རྩ་འགྲེལ་སྦྱོར་བའི་ཆུ་གཏེར་ཆེ། ། ལེགས་བཤད་ཡིད་བཞིན་ནོར་བུས་རབ་ཏུ་གཏམ། ། སྐལ་བཟང་ཀླུ་དབང་དགའ་བའི་རྣམ་འགྱུར་གྱིས། ། རོལ་པའི་མཚོ་ཆེན་བདག་གིས་བྲི་བར་བྱ། །
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's own pledge-verse, which decodes every element of the title on the page above it — the two rnam bshad, the difficult points, the ocean, the fortunate nāga-lords. Found by direct search.
The identical title formula heading a different volume — proof that the words of p1 are a series title, and that the series reaches past the eight skabs. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: dedicatory verse at a volume-break in the collected སྤྱི་དོན།
quotes.why: An unattributed dedication verse recurring at volume-breaks; it names the work by the short title ཀླུ་དབང་རོལ་མཚོ and glosses it as joining sūtra, Ornament and commentary. Found by direct search.
Ngok Lotsāwa's title has the same base object, the same task of clarifying its dka' ba'i gnas, and the same རོལ་མཚོ image — the model p1's title is built on. Found by direct search.
The first of the two rnam bshad, and the source of p1's phrase རྒྱན་འགྲེལ་པ་དང་བཅས་པ, which Chökyi Gyaltsen takes over verbatim. Found by direct search.
The second of the two rnam bshad; its own title shows it is a rnam bshad on Haribhadra's འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ, which fixes what the འགྲེལ་པ of p1's title refers to. Found by direct search.
The root text's own Tibetan title, of which p1 quotes the tail བསྟན་བཅོས་མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན. Found by direct search.
Haribhadra's short commentary calls itself simply the འགྲེལ་པ on the Ornament — the referent of p1's འགྲེལ་པ་དང་བཅས་པ. Found by direct search.
The Drepung Loseling yig cha's title page: the same opening formula as p1, but resting on one rnam bshad instead of two. Found by direct search.
A third Gelug rnam bshad on the same base, by Khedrup Je, which p1's count of two leaves out. Found by direct search.
His biographer describes the very method p1's title announces — spyi don worked over the ṭīkās of Tsongkhapa and his sons, settling the difficult points. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: རྣམ་ཐར་དངོས་གྲུབ་ཆར་འབེབས། the dream of Gyaltsab Je
quotes.why: The hagiography's account of how he came by the difficult points of the second rnam bshad — the title's own claim, told as vision. Found by direct search.
The catalogue of his writings records the Phar phyin spyi don as complete except for a small unfinished remainder of the very skabs this volume covers. Found by direct search.
Ties the genre pair mtha' dpyod / spyi don to the dka' gnad of a base text, which is what section 6 needs to define སྤྱི་དོན. Found by direct search.

The companion volume on the same skabs carries a wholly different title and calls itself notes taken from his speech — which is what makes p1's series title a claim about authorship. Found by direct search.
Tsongkhapa's account of Nāgārjuna bringing the Prajñāpāramitā sūtras out of the nāga realm — the second resonance available in the title's nāga imagery. Found by direct search.
